CAMERON WINTER AT CARNEGIE HALL in 35mm

Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a show at Carnegie Hall. One night only. This is the movie. Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar®-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (ONE BATTLE AFTER ANOTHER), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (THE SMASHING MACHINE) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy® winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). "Fallen Angels" by Noël Coward

Sparkling, dizzying and deliciously potent, “Fallen Angels,” Noël Coward’s champagne-fresh comedy of bad manners, shocked and delighted audiences at its 1925 premiere. Two upper-class wives, their husbands away for the day, share a few toasts to their premarital dalliances — with the same man, who just may be en route from France to visit. Old rivalries and past scandals bubble to the surface in this intoxicating romp from one of theater’s comedy masters. THE ADVENTURES OF PRINCE ACHMED

Lotte Reiniger’s trademark silhouette animation style brings “The Arabian Nights” to wondrous life in this enchanting film, hailed as the first feature-length animated film when it premiered in Germany in 1926. A wicked sorcerer tricks Prince Achmed into mounting a magical flying horse, which is intended to carry him to his death. But the prince foils the magician’s plan and soars headlong into a series of wondrous adventures — joining forces with Aladdin and the Witch of the Fiery Mountains, doing battle with the sorcerer’s army of monsters and demons and falling in love with the beautiful Princess Peri Banu.... read more
